nodes.text: …One moment. A fletch set wrong kills someone eight weeks from now, far from here. …There. Done. Now — you have my whole attention.

Ten years under Kestrel's banner, walking the High Road with a lamp and a bow. The road gave me back with a knee that predicts weather, and one rule: _never send anyone into the dark with gear you wouldn't stake your own life on._ I can't walk the miles anymore. So the miles come to my counter instead.

The watch on the wall. The castle guard. Kestrel's sergeants. Any honest traveler with coin and sense. When a watchman on the night wall nocks one of mine, he's holding my word that it flies true. I fletch like their lives depend on it. I remember when mine did.

Straight grain — the saw yard saves me its best billets. Feathers matched from the *same wing*, or the arrow corkscrews. And patience at the finish — the last touch is the one somebody's life leans on. That's the whole craft. Grain, feather, patience.
Fly straight. And thank the goose — everyone forgets the goose.
